role: Executive Director, South Carolina Wildlife and Marine Resources Department
stance_basis: two letters explicitly stating the S.C. Wildlife and Marine Resources Department opposes construction of the project
summary: James A. Timmerman, Jr., Executive Director of the South Carolina Wildlife and Marine Resources Department, submitted multiple letters opposing the Bad Creek Pumped Storage Project. His concerns centered on the destruction of trout streams, threats to the two-story trout fishery in Lake Jocassee, disruption of a unique spawning run in Howard Creek, inadequate data to support conclusions in the DEIS, and poor land use practices by Duke Power Company. He requested a delay in licensing and stated opposition unless additional information resolved the uncertainties.
complaint_summary: Timmerman requests an extension of time to January 15, 1976, to comment on the DEIS, citing concern about the effects of Bad Creek reservoir discharge on Lake Jocassee stratification and the need to await EPA comments on a Clemson University model report.

statement.text:
In reference to your letter of September 30, 1975, and the attached Draft Environmental Impact Statement for the Bad Creek Project No. 2740-South Carolina, I am providing the following comments.
An excellent two-story fishery has been created in Lake Jocassee. The effects of the discharge from the Bad Creek reservoir on the stratification of Lake Jocassee has been discussed with Duke Power personnel. During these discussions, we expressed our concern and requested a statement from Duke, based on engineering and biological research that this project would not alter or seriously alter stratification in Lake Jocassee.
A report, "Effects of Bad Creek Pumped Storage on Stratification in Lake Jocassee", was prepared for Duke Power Company by Billy L. Edge, Associate Professor, Department of Civil Engineering, Clemson University, Clemson, South Carolina, with the use of a physical model.
We have forwarded a copy of this report to the Environmental Protection Agency requesting their comments on this report in regard to our concern with lake stratification. We have not received their comments, therefore, would like to request an extension of time for our comments on the Draft Statement.
By copy of this letter, the South Carolina Wildlife and Marine Resources Department requests an extension of time to January 15, 1976, for providing our comments on the Draft Environmental Impact Statement, Bad Creek Project No. 2740-South Carolina.

summary_quote: With the uncertainty surrounding this proposed project and the importance of the resource endangered by the project, the S. C. Wildlife and Marine Resources Department opposes the construction of this project at this time.
